result.title: Model What Matters: Decision-Guided Selective World Modeling for Language Agents
result.comment: Core implementation included as ancillary files
result.summary: Reinforcement learning provides a direct mechanism for optimizing task objectives in large language model-driven agents, but task rewards are typically sparse trajectory-level signals that only evaluate task success, without directly supervising action-conditioned environment transitions, leaving the model with limited explicit understanding of action consequences and environment dynamics. Recent work introduces auxiliary supervision through policy and world modeling co-training, yet typically treats complete environmental observations uniformly as world modeling targets, overlooking the varying decision relevance of observation content. We propose DGS-WM (Decision-Guided Selective World Modeling), a decision-guided policy-world modeling co-training approach for language agents. DGS-WM employs a Decision-Guided Observation Selection component that filters observation units with decision value as world modeling targets based on their support for subsequent policy responses, and a Confidence-Adaptive Weighting component that adaptively adjusts supervision strength according to the model's prediction confidence on selected targets. Together, these components form a decision-aware auxiliary world modeling loss, jointly optimized with the RL loss on the same policy model. Across multiple benchmarks covering single-hop/multi-hop question answering and interactive web tasks, DGS-WM achieves consistent improvements under different model scales and RL algorithms, demonstrating more stable and effective performance compared to full-observation world modeling methods.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DGS-WM：在语言智能体的策略与世界模型联合训练中，依据观测单元对后续策略回答的支持程度筛选具决策价值的世界建模目标，并按模型预测置信度自适应调整监督强度，形成决策感知的辅助损失，在多跳问答与交互式网页任务上优于全观测世界建模。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按决策价值筛选观测单元 + 置信度自适应加权」的辅助监督思路，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、latent 状态监督的贡献分配相关，可供核查是否迁移到多模态观测单位的选择与加权。
